# **Requirement-to-Concept Trace**

| Requirement | Concept | State/behaviour | Decision |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Register patient | patient | Create a patient tuple and add their data | Keep |
| View patient details | Patient, practitioner | Open patient tuple | Keep |
| Create appointment | Appointment, patient, practitioner | Create an appointment and fill required data (time, practitioner, patient) | Keep |
| Cancel appointment | clinic | Take patients information and cancel appointment | Keep |
| Store/view appointment details | Clinic, practitioner | Store and save details for viewing | Keep |
| Register practitioner | practitioner | Create a practitioner tuple and add and save their data. | Keep |
| View practitioner details | Practitioner, receptionist | Open practitioner tuple | Keep |
| Patient search | Practitioner, receptionist | Search patient file for specific patient | Keep |
| Error handling for invalid operations | All | Error please try again | Keep |
| Appointment status | Practitioner,receptionist, patient, appointment | Check appointments and view what is happening at a certain time&nbsp; | Keep |

# **Design Rationale**

Explain class selection, responsibility allocation and key relationships.

The classes I selected are Clinic, appointment, Practitioner and patient as they are the ones using the system and they are each responsible for different parts of the process. Patient and practitioner are both related to the appointment as the appointment needs one patient and one practitioner. Patient and practitioner are both related to each other as they both need to view details about each other.

All the classes are then related back to the clinic as the appointments happen at the clinic and the clinic management needs to view appointment history for Operational reports and the receptionist on shift will need to be able to book and cancel appointments when a patient calls or comes in.
